sources.name: fineweb2-urd_Arab
sources.notes: 6.87 GB of parquet for a ~120M clean token target, so the default fetch takes the smaller train shard (order 0) plus the eval shard and stops. Shard 001 alone holds 1,547,542 documents averaging ~2,240 chars (~3.5G chars pre-filter), roughly 10x the target. CHECKED 2026-08-03: shards are NOT dump-partitioned — 88 distinct CommonCrawl dumps spanning CC-MAIN-2019-43 to CC-MAIN-2024-18 appear across the shard, and every row group mixes several — so one shard is not a time-biased slice. BUT documents are not shuffled either: row group 0 skews to 2021/2022 dumps and row group 206 to 2024, so a PREFIX of the shard is time-biased. Document selection at stage 9 and for arm A's 25M subsample must be random across the shard, never a prefix or contiguous block, or arm A becomes systematically older web text than arm B. The `test` shard is FineWeb2's own held-out slice of the same crawl; it is NOT a decontaminated eval set for us (stage 8 still applies).

sources.name: roman-urdu-parl
sources.role: Parallel script pairs, and the reference transliteration test split (PRD §6.2, §8.2)
sources.citation: Alam & Hussain, Roman-Urdu-Parl; split by Mavkif
sources.notes: PRD §6.2 warning applies: substantially machine-produced. ~6.37M pairs collapse to ~1.09M unique Urdu sentences, so the native side must be deduplicated hard (stage 6/7) before it enters pretraining, and any transliteration score on the reference split means 'matches that transliterator'. The human-written set in §8.2 exists to close that gap. Eval splits are ordered first so they can be fetched without the 1.19 GB train file.

rejected.name: UrduLM / ALIF Urdu Corpus
rejected.reason: The 33 GB corpus is not actually released. The public artifact is a 5,000-row / 14.5 MB preview; the paper's 'released openly' claim is not met for the corpus. Licence was never the blocker.
rejected.notes: Checked 2026-08-03. The arXiv paper is CC BY-NC-ND-4.0, but that covers the paper, not the data; the preview dataset is CC BY-SA-4.0 and the ALIF-Base-100M model is Apache-2.0. Retained as the PRD §6.1 'how much could we have collected' citation, WITH a qualification the report must carry: of the claimed 33 GB, 5.5 GB is English FineWeb machine-translated to Urdu via Google Translate and 19.4 GB is CommonCrawl, which overlaps Ravaan's own primary source. The ~5-6B-token figure is therefore not 5-6B tokens of independent, human-authored Urdu. Finding B's conclusion survives — even after discounting, collectable Urdu exceeds the ~1.4B Chinchilla-optimal budget for 70M params by several times — but the headline number must be stated with that caveat. Separately useful for Week 5: orature/ALIF-Base-100M is Apache-2.0 and ships a 32k Urdu SentencePiece model, a legitimate external fertility baseline for PRD §7.

rejected.name: CulturaX / OSCAR / ROOTS / Makhzan / Bactrian-X
rejected.reason: Dropped in PRD v2 §6.2: each costs weeks of integration and adds little on top of FineWeb2 for a ~120M-token target.
rejected.notes: Not a licence or quality judgement. If stage 5 filtering yields under the G1 threshold of 100M tokens, the first fallback is FineWeb2's second train shard, not a new source — adding a source changes the corpus mix and would confound arm A against arm B.
